title: Fields of Elation
era_role: Second movement of One: represents the 'honeymoon' phase or mystical ecstasy promised by Sleep, yet already tainted by the melancholy of loss ('losing touch') as the dream fades upon waking.
in_character_quotes_gap_reason: Sleep Token granted very few interviews in 2016-2018 and never provided track-by-track in-character commentary.

editorial_reading.summary: Critics and retrospectives highlight the contrast between Vessel's vulnerable falsetto and syncopated riffs: ecstasy ('elation') is not stable peace, but chemical dependency on an altered state.
editorial_reading.source_title: Louder - The story behind every Sleep Token song

editorial_reading.summary: Maintaining the themes of Thread The Needle, Fields Of Elation deals with adorationtinged toxicity. ‘The daylight recedes in unison. This room buries the hours like death,’ Vessel says at the start of the song. He could be referencing sex, staying in a bedroom while the sun sets, but as Fields Of Elation proceeds from subtle industrial music to heaving metal, the lyrics take on a horrible dependent edge.
editorial_reading.source_title: Louder - The story behind every Sleep Token song (Page 1)

editorial_reading.summary: “Thread the Needle” and “Fields of Elation” from One seem to document the initial identification and seduction of Vessel as a candidate. It’s important to note that all of the songs can be viewed through either a realistic or allegorical lens. Take instance “Thread the Needle”, which can be viewed as both an overtly erotic track or a metaphysical unification of Sleep and Vessel. The French have an expression, la petite mort, which in many ways reconciles this and represents the eventual rebirth of Vessel. Vessel finds a deep pleasure in Sleep, which the track illustrates on multiple fronts: “we can spend the night in fascination” (Vessel would be fascinated by all the things Sleep could teach him, and Sleep might also find Vessel himself fascinating); “something to confide in” (Sleep offering comfort and the promise of support to a character who seems to have nothing and no-one); “something to erase” (either something in Vessel’s past, or his worries and feelings of being lost. Perhaps, in the long run, his identity). Sleep entices Vessel with love bombing, the affection he has been starved of.
editorial_reading.source_title: Boolin Tunes - The Lore of Sleep Token

editorial_reading.summary: “Bury me inside this labyrinth bed” perhaps indicates Sleep’s co-dependency on his Vessels, making them almost like a tomb. Since Vessel is lost, his mind is a labyrinth. “You turn the lights down, come and find out,” is potentially the most multifarious line in the song: there is the obvious, sensual connotation, but also turning down the lights indicates Vessel lying down to slip into dreams, wherein he can communicate with Sleep more easily. Additionally, perhaps Sleep hopes the ‘dimming’ of Vessel’s will allow him to take over. The nod to time dilation alludes to both dreams and what it feel like to be with a partner: everything else worldly falls away and only the moment matters. Fields of Elation shows this effect of this: without Sleep, Vessel is depressed – he feels dead already – and believes only Sleep can pull him out from his hole.
editorial_reading.source_title: Boolin Tunes - The Lore of Sleep Token

references.detail: The 'Fields of Elation' mirror the Elysian Fields, the otherworldly realm of the blessed associated with Hypnos (deity of sleep) and Thanatos.
references.supporting_phrase: Quietly, they're carving out my name / Across the fields of elation

callbacks.motif: The motif of the lost idyllic meadow/garden ('fields of elation') is the direct precursor to the pastoral topoi of Eden and Arcadia in chapters 3 and 4.
callbacks.source_title: Lore of Sleep Token - One EP

community_theories.theory: The imagery of a living burial ('shallow grave', 'carving out my name') is read by fans as the symbolic death of the singer's prior identity to become 'Vessel' (the empty container of Sleep).
community_theories.source_title: Sleep Token Collective Wiki - Fields of Elation

community_theories.theory: The EP consist of 3 songs, Thread The Needle, Fields Of Elation, and When The Bough Breaks. Before releasing the EP, the band had already debuted the song Thread The Needle as a single in September 8th, 2016.[1] The piano version of all 3 songs in the EP are available on Sleep Token's bandcamp.
Fields Of Elation is the second track from Sleep Token's first EP, One. Fields Of Elation released on November 10th, 2016 with it's official video.
community_theories.source_title: Sleep Token Collective Wiki - Fields of Elation
